course.title: Data and Code Management
course.subtitle: From Collection to Application
course.question: Can someone else understand, check, reproduce and use your work?
course.lede: You already know how to analyse. DCM asks the next question: whether your work survives contact with another person, another machine and another week. Code production is increasingly AI-assisted — code literacy and engineering judgement are what make the result trustworthy.

moodle.note: Moodle remains the official UNIL space for announcements, submissions, grades and the course forum. This public site carries the syllabus, schedule, slides and materials.

pillars.name: Code literacy
pillars.blurb: Read, explain, modify and debug code instead of only running it. Data structures, tables, control flow and functions — the literacy that lets you judge what an agent hands back.

pillars.name: Data
pillars.blurb: Relational data, SQL, joins and aggregation, JSON and web data. Trace provenance; validate keys, units, missing values and totals. Getting the data is only the start.

pillars.name: Engineering
pillars.blurb: Project structure, modular code, documentation, refactoring and tests, versioned and reviewed through Git and GitHub. More generated code makes review and structure more important, not less.

pillars.name: Production
pillars.blurb: Dependencies, reproducible environments and Docker, and a small data application someone else can actually open and use. From a working script to a project you can hand over.

ai.label: AI throughout
ai.tagline: Support at every stage — not a fifth block

growth.title: Explain & debug
growth.text: Predict, write and explain short code before delegating any of it.

growth.title: Generate & refactor
growth.text: Specify bounded changes, then inspect the diff before you run it.

growth.title: Test, review & build
growth.text: Coordinate larger tasks and carry the evidence that the result is right.

journey.name: Notebook
journey.text: An analysis that runs on your machine, in your session, with your assumptions.

journey.name: Workflow
journey.text: Validated inputs, reusable steps, tests and checks, and a fixed environment.

journey.name: Application
journey.text: A reproducible project and a small product another person can open and trust.

outcomes.title: Code you can explain
outcomes.text: Read, modify and debug Python/R inside a reproducible project.

outcomes.title: Data you can trust
outcomes.text: Work with files, databases and APIs, and validate every transformation.

outcomes.title: A project others can maintain
outcomes.text: Structure, document and test code; collaborate through Git.

outcomes.title: A result others can use
outcomes.text: Reproduce the environment and deliver a small application.

assessment.label: Homework 1
assessment.name: Human handover
assessment.question: Can another person understand and reproduce your work?
assessment.summary: Code literacy and reproducibility: explain and debug code, structure a project, show tests, Git history and evidence of a fresh rerun.

assessment.label: Homework 2
assessment.name: Technical handover
assessment.question: Can the workflow run reliably outside your own setup?
assessment.summary: Data through to production: SQL and data validation, modular and testable code, environments and Docker where appropriate.

assessment.label: Group project
assessment.name: User handover
assessment.question: Can a team deliver something another person can actually use?
assessment.summary: Full integration of all four stages into a usable data product, with checked results, defended choices and AI-assisted development you can account for.

evidence.title: Explain
evidence.text: The code, the data's meaning, your assumptions and the limits.

evidence.title: Validate
evidence.text: Tests, checks and independent evidence — not just “it ran”.

evidence.title: Reproduce
evidence.text: Inputs, instructions, dependencies and a fresh run that still works.

evidence.title: Defend
evidence.text: The choices you made, your contribution and the changes you reviewed.

evidence.title: Account for AI
evidence.text: Appropriate assistance, independent verification and disclosure.

tools.name: VS Code

tools.name: AI coding agent

tools.name: Streamlit / Shiny

schedule.title: Special workshops
schedule.summary: No normal DCM class. Thesis and career workshops run in this slot.

schedule.title: Introduction: DCM in 2026
schedule.summary: What the course is for, the four-stage map, AI throughout, assessment, and a first look at the inspect → specify → verify workflow with a coding agent.
schedule.prep: Complete the minimum setup checks before class — see Setup.

schedule.title: Reproducibility, projects, Git/GitHub
schedule.summary: Project structure, immutable raw data, relative paths and READMEs; Git basics — status, diff, staged changes, commits — and a reviewed change you can explain.

schedule.title: Code literacy I
schedule.summary: Types, missing values, vectors and tables, indexing and logical operations. Predict what code does before you run it.

schedule.title: Code literacy II
schedule.summary: Control flow, functions, input checks, errors and warnings — and reading, modifying and debugging code you did not write.

schedule.title: Responsible AI at UNIL
schedule.summary: Asynchronous session on institutional guidance for AI use, including UNIL resources such as AI_GO. No class meeting in the room.

schedule.title: SQL & relational data
schedule.summary: Relational thinking, SELECT, joins and aggregation, and calling SQL from Python/R — plus checking that a query means what you think it means.

schedule.title: APIs, JSON & web data
schedule.summary: Requesting data from APIs, reading JSON, handling keys and rate limits, and validating external data before you build on it.

schedule.title: Software engineering with AI
schedule.summary: Functions and modules, documentation, refactoring and tests — and how to specify, review and test work produced with an agent.

schedule.title: Environments & Docker
schedule.summary: Dependencies and environments, why “works on my machine” is not a result, and a first reproducible container.

schedule.title: Applications + project kickoff
schedule.summary: Turning a workflow into a small application someone else can use, and the launch of the group project.

schedule.title: Project work I
schedule.summary: Supervised project work: scope, data, structure and a first end-to-end path.

schedule.title: Project work II + review
schedule.summary: Supervised project work and a review round: does the project run for someone else?

schedule.title: Project presentations
schedule.summary: Final presentations: show the product, the checks behind it and the choices you defend.
